correctness.rationale: The pair partition yields density (1) with exact normalization. Its origin value and first right derivative are 2/L and k(k-3)/L^2; for k>=3 the second expression uniquely identifies k. The distributional second derivative has negative single-arm atoms and positive pair-sum atoms. After canceling contributions of recovered arm copies, the least remaining support point is necessarily the least unrecovered arm and has mass -(k-2) times its multiplicity, proving collision-safe induction. k=1,2 are intervals determined by L. The included checker verifies 77 exact rational inversion/normalization examples and 230 exact kink masses, including resonant and repeated lengths, and simulates 140000 pairs; these computations do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Complete recovery of an unknown number of positive real arm lengths from one natural global metric-measure invariant is a structural inverse classification. It is not a rephrasing of labeled distance-matrix recovery, because all endpoint labels and pair identities are integrated out; nonisometric metric trees can share global or local distance distributions. The finite signed-kink recursion resolves all resonance cases, clarifies exactly the unavoidable artificial degree-two ambiguity and gives a reproducible reconstruction algorithm. No statistical stability or general-tree injectivity is inferred.
